en.title: Output All Pairs with the Minimum Absolute Difference
en.description:
Given distinct integers, find all unordered pairs with the minimum absolute difference. In each pair the smaller number comes first, and all pairs are output in ascending order by the first item, then by the second.

The standard input/output format was compiled by this site; added numeric bounds and the encoding for no-solution cases are explicitly marked and do not claim to be the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains distinct integers. 2≤n≤100000, −10^9≤value≤10^9.
en.output: Output the number of pairs on the first line, followed by two integers per line in the specified order.
en.explanation: The examples give only -1 0; 3 4, 4 5, 5 6, 6 7; and 1 3, 3 5 respectively. The wrong answer in the original site's first example has been corrected according to the statement body.
hints: Sort, find the minimum difference between adjacent elements, then output every adjacent pair whose difference equals it.
